chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from whoever narrated to him, he said:

Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) would not ask whether the child was male or female when he was informed of a birth, until he said, 'Is he sound/healthy?' When it was said that he was sound, he would say, 'Praise be to Allah who did not create from me something deformed.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn ask first when hearing about a new birth?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration highlights Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn’s (AS) pragmatic gratitude, prioritizing physical soundness (*sawi*) over gender, which reflects a Shia emphasis on valuing the child's inherent health rather than societal preferences. His specific supplication acknowledges that while Allah creates all, He is the source of perfection, distinguishing between mere existence and the absence of defect. This practice underscores the ethical principle of accepting divine decree with contentment regarding the child's physical state.
